To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the opportunity to destroy the Klingons was a conditioned reinforcer and that observing behavior is maintained by a schedule of reinforcement.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the observer in a social situation.
the role of conditioned reinforcement in the acquisition and maintenance of observing behavior in an operant task.
the reinforcement properties of events in a computer game, "ST," and the effects of these events on observing behavior.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the results of the experiment were in accord with the predictions of the conditioned reinforcement theory and inconsistent with the uncertainty-reduction theory.
the results are consistent with the hypothesis that observing responses are maintained by the conditioned reinforcement of information.
the data do not support the uncertainty-reduction view of observing behavior, but they are not incompatible with it.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
observing responses are not maintained by the information per se, but by the conditioned reinforcement of information that can be used to advantage in obtaining other types of reinforcement.
observing is maintained by conditioned reinforcement, and that conditioned reinforcement is more effective when the information it provides can be used to advantage in the situation.

the more a stimulus was correlated with the opportunity to obtain the reinforcers, the more observing responses it maintained, but only if the information could be used to advantage with regard to those reinforcers. (Author/Author abstract)
The main takeaway from our work is that
the contingencies studied in lever press procedures can be incorporated into a computer game.

the contingencies of reinforcement that are studied in a laboratory setting can be incorporated into a popular game and studied under naturalistic conditions. This is an important finding for the field of psychology and

the reinforcement hypothesis of observing is more likely to be supported when the information provided is useful for making decisions about the contingencies of reinforcement in a situation than when the information is not useful.
